title: First Entry into a Stopping Set
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine, let $S$ be its state set, and let $w$ be a Boolean input word. Suppose a predicate $P$ on states has the property that every configuration whose state satisfies $P$ is fixed by one step of $M$. If configurations $c$ and $d$ and a time bound $T$ satisfy that $d$ has a state satisfying $P$ and the run from $c$ reaches $d$ after $T$ steps, then there is a time $t\le T$ at which the run from $c$ is $d$, with no earlier time $j<t$ at which its state satisfies $P$.
hypotheses_covered: A multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and state set $S$
Every configuration with a state satisfying $P$ is fixed by one step
The run from $c$ reaches $d$ after $T$ steps
replaced:
Let a class of control states be absorbing (any configuration whose state
lies in the class is a fixed point of the step function), and suppose the
run from $c$ reaches a configuration $d$ with state in the class after $T$
steps. Then there is a time $t \le T$ with no earlier visit to the class
such that the configuration at time $t$ is already $d$.
